'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[COVID-19 recession]]
***[[France]]'s [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] [[recession|contracts]] 8.3% in 2020, the country's worst [[Economy of France|economic performance]] since [[World War II]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210129-covid-19-pandemic-pushes-french-economy-into-deep-recession (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], COVID-19 recession
***[[Spain]]'s GDP contracts 11% in 2020, the country's worst [[Economy of Spain|economic performance]] since the [[Spanish Civil War]]. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/spain-beats-forecasts-with-04-rise-in-gdp-2021-01-29 (Marketwatch)]
 
'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[January 31 – February 3, 2021 nor'easter|February 2021 nor'easter]]
**A [[winter storm]] causes [[Mudflow|mudslide]]s in [[southern California]], resulting in over 50 car accidents. [https://abc7.com/weather/powerful-storm-drenches-socal;-multiple-mudslides-accidents-reported/10122294/ (KABC-TV)]
**The [[National Weather Service]] issued a [[Winter Storm Warning]] for all areas above 6,500 feet (1,981 meters) in [[Nevada]]. [https://www.weather.gov/wwamap/wwatxtget.php?cwa=rev&wwa=all (National Weather Service)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
**Fifteen people are killed in a [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] facility due to a fire at the Matei Balș Hospital in [[Bucharest]], [[Romania]]. [https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/actualitate/sanatate/un-nou-deces-in-randul-pacientilor-transferati-din-pavilionul-afectat-de-incendiul-de-la-matei-bals-1447984 (Digi 24)]
*A [[Aviation accidents and incidents|helicopter crashes]] against a hill in eastern [[Cuba]], killing all five people onboard. [http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/latestnews/Five_dead_in_Cuba_helicopter_crash,_official?profile=1228 (AFP via ''Jamaica Observer'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
*****[[Arizona]] reports the first three cases of the UK variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona-health/2021/01/29/uk-variant-b-117-of-new-coronavirus-has-been-confirmed-in-arizona/4314245001/ (''The Arizona Republic'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delaware]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
*****[[Delaware]] reports the first case of the B.1.1.7 variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in three people from [[New Castle County, Delaware|New Castle County]]. [https://news.delaware.gov/2021/01/29/delaware-division-of-public-health-confirms-first-covid-19-cases-with-the-uk-variant/ (Delaware Government)]
****The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] issues a rule requiring all travelers using [[Public transportation in the United States|public transportation]] to wear a mask while boarding, during the trip, and while disembarking. The rule also states face shields, bandanas, and scarves are not permissible forms of face covering. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/01/30/cdc-public-transportation-face-mask-order-463969 (''Politico'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] and major Canadian airlines agree to suspend all flights to "sun destinations" such as the [[Caribbean]] and [[Mexico]] until April 30. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-55863882 (BBC News)]
****Trudeau announces new measures to take effect "in the coming weeks" that will require incoming travelers to undergo mandatory [[COVID-19 testing#Reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction|PCR testing]] upon arrival and [[quarantine]] in a hotel for a maximum of three days at their own expense. [https://apnews.com/article/cananda-coronavirus-travel-21d1685b076a62025326b0eb4441cd9c (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Prime Minister of France|Prime Minister]] [[Jean Castex]] announces the closure of borders to all travelers outside the [[European Union]] beginning January 31 in order to reduce the spread of [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|SARS-CoV-2 variants]] and avoid a third [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]]. In addition, travel between the [[Overseas territories of France|overseas territories]] will be limited and all large shopping centres will be closed. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/france-close-borders-arrivals-eu-75570659 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The German [[Federal Ministry of the Interior, Building and Community|Ministry of Interior]] bans entry to all travellers from the [[United Kingdom]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], [[Brazil]], [[Portugal]], and [[South Africa]] from tomorrow until February 17 in order to reduce the spread of [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|SARS-CoV-2 variants]]. In addition, travellers from [[Lesotho]] and [[Eswatini]] will also be banned beginning January 31. [https://www.dpa-international.com/topic/germany-imposes-travel-bans-regions-feared-virus-variants-urn%3Anewsml%3Adpa.com%3A20090101%3A210129-99-227128 (Dpa International)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] delays the reopening of high schools, which was scheduled to begin on February 1, due to an increase in the number of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases, particularly in red zone areas. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/261798/article/ekathimerini/news/greece-delays-school-reopening-plans-after-covid-19-infections-rise (''Ekathimerini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] approves the Chinese-made [[Sinopharm]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for use in the country, becoming the first [[European Union|EU]] member state to do so. [https://www.dw.com/en/hungary-approves-chinese-covid-vaccine/a-56382425 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****The [[Verkhovna Rada]] passes a law banning registration of the [[Sputnik V]] [[vaccine]] developed by [[Russia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/healthcoronavirus-ukraine-vaccine/update-1-ukraine-bans-use-of-russian-covid-19-vaccines-idUSL1N2K40V2 (Reuters)]
***The [[European Medicines Agency]] approves the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca Vaccine]] for use within the EU and recommends that the [[European Commission]] grant it 'limited marketing authorization' within the union. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/29/astrazeneca-oxford-vaccine-approved-for-use-by-european-regulator.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 5,725 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 203,933. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/01/29/covid-19-record-5725-new-cases-reported-16-deaths-bring-death-toll-to-733 (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[Presidential Communications Group#Presidential Spokesperson|Presidential Spokesperson]] [[Harry Roque]] announces that the [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines|General Community Quarantine]] (GCQ) in [[Metro Manila]] will be extended until February 28 and also places the [[Cordillera Administrative Region]] under GCQ status because most of the cases of the B.1.1.7 variant have been reported in the region. [https://www.cnnphilippines.com/news/2021/1/29/Philippines-community-quarantine-Metro-Manila-GCQ-February.html (CNN Philippines)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****The [[Government of Thailand|government]] announces that [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] restrictions will be eased in most areas of the [[Thailand|country]] beginning February 1, allowing some businesses to reopen and restaurants to extend their operating hours. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2059315/covid-control-restrictions-eased-from-monday (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkmenistan]]
****[[Turkmenistan]] approves the [[EpiVacCorona]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], becoming the first country outside of [[Russia]] to do so. [https://business.com.tm/post/6607/turkmenistan-approves-use-of-russias-epivaccorona-vaccine (Business TM)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***Pharmaceutical company [[Johnson & Johnson]] announces their single-dose COVID-19 vaccine is 66% effective in preventing moderate disease and 85% in preventing severe disease during a global trial. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/01/29/johnson-and-johnson-vaccine-efficacy-coronavirus-463732 (''Politico'')]
***[[Novartis]] signs an agreement with [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]] to help produce their [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-01-novartis-pfizer-biontech-covid-vaccine.html (MedicalXpress)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] signs a bill extending the [[New START]] [[Nuclear disarmament|nuclear arms reduction]] treaty with the [[United States]] until 2026, ahead of its expiration date next week, following talks with [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jan/29/putin-signs-last-minute-extension-to-nuclear-weapons-treaty-with-us (''The Guardian'')]
*[[China–Vanuatu relations]]
**A [[Vanuatu]] [[patrol boat]] detains two [[Fishing industry in China|Chinese fishing]] vessels near the [[Torres Islands]] in the [[Coral Sea]] for suspected [[Illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing|illegal fishing]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jan/26/chinese-vessels-detained-by-vanuatu-accused-of-fishing-illegally (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Criminal proceedings in the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Criminal charges brought in the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
***Two members of the [[Proud Boys]] are charged with conspiracy to [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|breach]] the [[United States Capitol]], including one of the members seen smashing a window with a police shield. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/29/nyregion/proud-boys-charged-with-conspiracy-in-capitol-riot.html (''New York Times'')]
***The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] announces that two women are arrested in [[Pennsylvania]] for their roles in the January 6 riot. One of the women, Dawn Bancroft, made threats to shoot [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/capitol-riot-arrests-pelosi-threat-b1795124.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[crime in the United Kingdom]]
**Migrants [[Arson|set fire]] to the Napier [[Barracks]] at [[Shorncliffe Army Camp]] in [[Kent]] after "reports of a disturbance". The [[Home Office]] says people "set about destroying the barracks", after being told that they were being moved due to a COVID-19 outbreak at the camp. [[Kent Police]] say that the fire caused "a significant amount of damage" and is investigating it as a suspected [[arson]] attack. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-kent-55863081 (BBC News)]
*[[Legality of euthanasia]]
**The [[Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)|parliament]] of [[Portugal]] passes legislation to legalize [[euthanasia]]. [https://www.rte.ie/news/2021/0129/1193783-portugal-euthanasia-law/ (AFP via RTE)]
*[[Crime in France]]
**A man is arrested after being linked to the [[murder]]s of three women and the wounding of a man in the past three days in and around [[Valence, Drôme|Valence]], [[France]]. The victims, who were shot in four separate locations, were [[Human resource management|HR managers]]; the attacker's motives are suspected to be linked to his earlier employment. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-55854459 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Death of Brian Sicknick]], [[aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]] and [[Senate Majority Leader]] [[Chuck Schumer]] announce that Brian Sicknick, the [[United States Capitol Police]] officer who died from injuries sustained during the [[2021 storming of the United States Capitol|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]], will [[Lying in state#United States|lie in honor]] at the [[United States Capitol rotunda|Rotunda]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-55866716 (BBC News)]
